title: Quotinator Per-Source Conflict-Resolution Rule File
description: A minimal, hand-authored set of rules (#181) that auto-resolve a field for a specific entity (Quote, Series, Universe, or any other type whose planner wires in ConflictRuleLookup) instead of leaving it staged Pending under the review duplicate-resolution policy. One rule file per bundled source, referenced from that source's own manifest.json entry via ruleFile. #153 (Phase 2) will later add a generated, declarative form of this same file shape.

rules.description: Every entity this file declares a rule for. Empty for a source with no known recurring conflicts. Grouped by entity (one entry per entity), not flattened to one entry per field — a single entity can have more than one field in conflict at once. A single rules array can mix ids from more than one entity type (e.g. a Quote id alongside a Series id).

entityId.description: The entity's own id (matched case-insensitively, per this project's id-comparison convention).

existingRecord.description: The existing (already-seeded) side's complete field set, recorded at the time this rule was authored — lets a human reviewing this file see the whole record, not only the field(s) actually being resolved. Purely documentation, never read by the matching logic.

incomingRecord.description: The incoming (this source file's own) side's complete field set, recorded at the time this rule was authored. See existingRecord.

fields.description: Every field of this entity that this rule file resolves. Not limited to fields that actually disagree between the two sides — a Custom rule can also correct a field that's simply wrong or missing on both.

field.description: The field name this rule governs (e.g. 'date', 'type', 'source', 'quoteText', 'character', 'author', 'originalLanguage', 'genres') — a key present in both existingRecord and incomingRecord.

resolution.description: Keep — resolve to the existing (already-seeded) side's value. Replace — resolve to the incoming (this file's own) value. Custom — resolve to customValue, a value neither side actually has (e.g. correcting a field that's missing from both, not just disagreed upon).

customValue.description: The value to use when resolution is Custom. Required when resolution is Custom; must be omitted otherwise.
